narrative_purpose: Anchor the cold open: the reader kneels in the dead ground with a handful of ash, confronting the chapter's central question — why is this still barren a generation on?
subject: A close low view of a blue-skinned Na'vi hand lifting and letting fall a handful of coarse grey volcanic ash, individual grains catching the dim light as they spill; no roots, no humus, no green in the ash.
scene: A barren ashland floor, the charred stump-skeleton of a giant Pandoran tree rising just behind, a faint fumarole leaking steam from a crack in the crust nearby, grey plain fading into haze beyond.
camera: Very close low ground-level shot on the hand and falling ash, shallow depth so the tree skeleton and fumarole sit soft behind.
light: Dim overcast light with a faint cool cyan cast; the only warmth a weak amber flush from the fumarole vapour.
palette: Stone-grey ash and indigo shadow dominant, a thread of ember-amber at the vent, almost no green.
style: Painterly naturalist plate, intimate and tactile, observed close.
detail_level: High detail on the hand and individual falling ash grains; background tree and vent soft in haze.
composition: Hand and spilling ash fill the lower foreground, tree skeleton upper background, fumarole to one side, dead negative space of grey plain.
consistency_notes: Same Ashlands world as the cover: grey tephra, calcined tree skeletons, fumaroles. Ash is lifeless and dry, clearly not soil.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no green vegetation, no neon, no photographic or 3D-render look, no cartoon style
